title: A Typewriter for the Uniform
premise: In the winter of 1938, Oscar Thornbury carries coded dispatches for a republic on the edge of collapse, hiding behind a courier's neutrality and ten years of practiced silence. When the mountain bridge closes for the season, they are stranded in the border town of Vellacorte with a dying typist named Ilse Brandt, who has been forging identity papers in her workshop above the bakery. To finish her work — and their own mission — Oscar must learn the trade of false names while soldiers close in, discovering that every document saved is a life risked and every silence kept is someone betrayed. The book ends with Oscar burning the workshop's ledgers, carrying one unfinished typewriter across the thawing river, and choosing at last to speak their own true name aloud.
about_author: S. M. Marchetti is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing displaced-persons records from interwar Europe. They write historical fiction about the small bureaucratic mercies that outlast the regimes that tried to forbid them.

chapters.title: The Courier's Silence
chapters.summary: Oscar crosses into Vellacorte with sealed dispatches sewn into a coat lining, narrating in close third person. A checkpoint interrogation establishes the rules of survival: answer less than asked, never more. The emotional beat is controlled dread — Oscar's competence masks how alone they are, and how much of themselves they've already surrendered to the role of nobody.

chapters.title: Bridge Out
chapters.summary: News arrives that the river bridge has closed for the season; avalanches have cut the only road south. POV shifts between Oscar and Ilse Brandt, the typist who watches the same snowfall from her workshop window. The beat is claustrophobic entrapment: two strangers realize the town that shelters them has become a trap with a timetable.

chapters.title: The Workshop Above the Bakery
chapters.summary: Seeking warmth, Oscar discovers Ilse's hidden trade: forged passports, baptismal records, and a battered typewriter whose keys don't match its typeface. She mistakes them for a customer; Oscar lets her. The emotional beat is temptation — for the first time, silence feels like complicity rather than safety.

chapters.title: Names Not Their Own
chapters.summary: Ilse bargains: she'll help Oscar move the dispatches if Oscar learns the typewriter and takes over when her hands fail — early tremors she hides badly. Through her lessons we learn whose names fill the ledgers. The beat is reluctant intimacy; two people teaching each other the grammar of survival.

chapters.title: What the Major Collects
chapters.summary: Occupying officer Major Reiner requisitions the bakery as a signals post, one floor below the workshop. He is courteous, observant, and collects confiscated typewriters. Oscar must deliver dispatches past his office daily. The beat is vertigo — danger now lives directly beneath them, listening through the floorboards.

chapters.title: Ten Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: A flashback chapter in Oscar's voice: the family lost, the first forged paper that saved them, the mentor who taught them that silence keeps people safe — and what it cost. Present-day Ilse reads Oscar's hesitation correctly. The beat is excavation; the buried self begins to surface.

chapters.title: A Knock at Midnight
chapters.summary: A hunted family arrives seeking papers; harboring them means the workshop cannot be moved or burned. Reiner's men search the building and find nothing by inches. Ilse collapses afterward — her illness is worse than she admitted. The beat is terror braided with tenderness; the stakes turn from documents to bodies.

chapters.title: The Ledger Must Burn
chapters.summary: With Ilse bedridden, Oscar faces the choice: the ledgers list everyone she ever helped, including the family upstairs. Reiner offers Oscar passage over the closed bridge in exchange for 'the typewriter and everything with it.' The beat is moral climax approaching — survival offered at the price of betrayal.

chapters.title: Fire on the Water
chapters.summary: Climax. Oscar feeds the ledgers to the bakery oven, triggering an alarm that covers the family's flight to the ice caves, while Ilse dies at her desk finishing one last name. Confronted by Reiner, Oscar speaks — truly speaks — for the first time, claiming the work as theirs. The beat is grief transfigured into witness.

chapters.title: One Unfinished Machine
chapters.summary: Resolution. Spring breaks the bridge open. Oscar crosses with the dispatches delivered and Ilse's unfinished typewriter strapped to their back, leaving the completed blank pages where the next forger will find them. In the border town beyond, asked their name by a clerk, Oscar answers with their own. The beat is inheritance accepted: silence ends, the name continues.
